records.text:
ECG: Initial electrocardiogram results were unremarkable.
Continuous Ambulatory ECG (14-day Zio XT monitor):  Image Title: Rhythm Strip From Zio Monitor  Image Description: The rhythm strip shows dual sinus node activity with:  - Donor sinus node rate estimated at 62 beats per minute  - Native sinus node rate estimated at 70 beats per minute  - A pause in ventricular activation interrupted by a junctional escape beat after 4.5 seconds  - Smaller P waves visible within the pause, dissociated from the active rhythm  - Prior 12-lead ECGs: Showed intermittent deflections with diminutive native P waves.

records.query: Need the patient's detailed medication list with doses and timing, serial blood pressure readings including orthostatic measurements, and cardiac evaluation results (echocardiogram, cardiac allograft vasculopathy status) to confirm medication-induced hypotension and assess the clinical significance of the 4.5-second pause on Zio monitoring.

Need the Zio monitor symptom event diary and patient-reported symptoms during the documented 4.5-second pause to confirm temporal correlation with dizziness/near-syncope, plus serial orthostatic blood pressure readings and current medication list with doses to assess the contributing hypotensive effect.

Need the Zio monitor symptom–event diary entries correlating the documented 4.5-second pause with dizziness/near-syncope, along with concurrent blood pressure readings and medication timing during that period, to confirm the arrhythmia as the symptomatic cause and clarify the contribution of amlodipine-related hypotension.

bindings.label: Patient experienced new-onset dizziness while sitting and episodes of near-syncope without loss of consciousness

Patient is a man in his 70s with a history of orthotopic heart transplant performed using the biatrial surgical technique; posttransplant history includes grade 1 cardiac allograft vasculopathy, toxic multinodular goiter status post-thyroidectomy, and tremors treated with propranolol
Two weeks prior, the cardiologist measured low blood pressure and stopped amlodipine treatment, after which symptoms improved
At presentation, physical examination showed the patient was normotensive and cardiac examination was unremarkable
Zio monitor recorded a 4.5-second ventricular pause with junctional escape and dual sinus activity
Ventricular pause/junctional escape arrhythmia is an independent cause of dizziness/near-syncope
No orthostatic blood pressure measurements were obtained during the evaluation
